issues.display_title: Issue #1207: Logout returns to the dashboard instead of the login page until a refresh
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Reported in chat (2026-10-12): after clicking Logout, MapThru stays on the dashboard, and only a page refresh brings up the login page.

Reproduce (production build)

  1. While signed in, open the landing page /.
  2. Click "Sign in". It takes you to /dashboard.
  3. Open the profile menu and click Logout.

/api/logout answers 204 and clears the session cookie, but the page goes back to /dashboard, the button stays on "Signing out…", and the login page only shows after a refresh. Opening the dashboard directly (a full page load) and logging out works.

It does not happen under next dev, which does not prefetch links.

Cause

  • The landing page links to /login and /register with <Link>, and a production build prefetches them while they are in view.
  • At that moment the visitor is still signed in, so the proxy (src/proxy.ts, signedOutOnlyPaths) answers the prefetch with a 307 to /dashboard. The client router keeps that redirect as the result for /login.
  • DashboardNav.handleLogout (src/components/dashboard/DashboardNav.tsx) calls requestSignOut() and then router.push("/login"). The client navigation reuses the cached redirect and lands on /dashboard, now signed out.
  • The verify-email-pending page has the same shape: it signs out, then calls router.push("/register").

This is on development as of 7ba9774a.

Scope

  1. After a sign-out, the next page is loaded in full (window.location) instead of through the client router. The navigation moves into the shared requestSignOut (src/lib/auth/signOut.ts), so both callers get it.
  2. Logout keeps its current order: analytics first, then /api/logout, then the navigation (#1086, #1091).

Acceptance criteria

  • Landing → Sign in → dashboard → Logout opens the login page without a refresh, in a production build.
  • Logout from a dashboard opened directly still opens the login page.
  • Sign out on the verify-email-pending page opens /register.

RESULT

video-1207-logout.mp4

Released to main in 613adec4 (release PR #1210). The fix came in through PR #1208, merged to development as 41613440; the fix commit is d330e257. Deploy succeeded.

Logout now opens the login page straight away, including when the dashboard was reached from the landing page's Sign in link. "Wrong email? Sign out" on verify-email-pending opens /register the same way.

Fix

  • src/lib/auth/signOut.ts: requestSignOut(to) calls /api/logout, then loads to in full with window.location.assign.
    • Before, the callers used router.push. That replayed the redirect to /dashboard the router had prefetched for /login while the visitor was still signed in.
  • src/components/dashboard/DashboardNav.tsx calls requestSignOut("/login"). router.push and setUser(null) are gone, because the full load resets every store.
  • src/app/(auth)/verify-email-pending/verify-pending-client.tsx calls requestSignOut("/register").
  • The sign-out analytics event is still sent: Countly keeps its queue in localStorage and sends it from the next page.

Tests

  • New src/lib/auth/__tests__/signOut.test.ts: the session ends first, then the next page loads in full. Dropping location.assign fails it.
  • DashboardNav.test.tsx: Logout calls requestSignOut("/login").
  • pnpm test (2974), pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit and next build pass.

Checked

  • Real Chrome against two local production builds, development against the fix: 4/4 (.playwright-mcp/demo/1207/check-logout.mjs).
    • development goes back to the dashboard, stuck on "Signing out…".
    • The fix opens /login from the landing flow and from a directly opened dashboard, and /register from verify-email-pending.
  • Production map-thru.com after the deploy: 5/5 (.playwright-mcp/demo/1207/check-prod.mjs).
    • The landing page still prefetches /login while signed in, answered with a 307 to /dashboard.
    • Sign in opens the dashboard.
    • Logout gets a 204 from /api/logout, opens /login (not the dashboard), and the session cookie is cleared.
  • Demo: .playwright-mcp/demo/1207/video-1207-logout.mp4.

issues.display_title: Issue #1211: Editor: walls near a door disappear on large plans (opening tolerance is 3 % of the plan)
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

From #1209 (2026-10-12). In the editor's 2D plan, some closed rooms show no wall line on part of their outline. The screenshot is Square One Mall V6 (Demo), Level 1: Big Fat Cookies, Escalators, Elevators and Washroom – Men's. Their horizontal walls are missing, while the vertical and slanted ones show.

Cause

The walls exist. The editor treats them as cut by a door that is far away.

  • The 2D plan (draw.ts, openTol) and the editor's 3D pane (scene3d.ts, tol) cut a wall at a door or window using a tolerance of 3 % of the plan's size.
  • doorSpanOnWall (floorplan/geometry.ts) cuts every wall that is roughly parallel to the opening when both of the opening's ends lie within that tolerance of the wall's line.
  • On a mall plan the tolerance is huge. Level 1 is 17 204 × 23 014 units, so 3 % is 690 units ≈ 34.5 m. One door at y = 12 613 erases the horizontal walls of the shops up to 330 units away from it.
  • The map already cuts openings at a fixed 0.6 m (geojson-utils.ts, 0.6 / mpp). The comment in draw.ts saying all three surfaces use the same tolerance is out of date.

Measured on Square One Mall V6:

Level Today (3 %) At 0.6 m
1 47 walls cut, 20 erased entirely 11 cut, 6 erased (walls with a door actually on them)
2 42 cut, 9 erased 8 cut, 4 erased

This is on development as of 41613440, and on production.

Scope

  1. The 2D plan and the editor's 3D pane cut openings at the map's tolerance, so the three surfaces agree again:
    • 0.6 m when the plan has a scale (600 / scaleMmPerUnit);
    • for an unscaled plan, the same share of the plan the map uses when it normalizes such a plan to 50 m (1.2 % of its larger side).
  2. One shared helper, so the two editor surfaces cannot drift apart again.
  3. A door or window that really sits on a wall still cuts it, in 2D and 3D.

Acceptance criteria

  • On Square One Mall V6, Level 1, Big Fat Cookies, Escalators, Elevators and Washroom – Men's show every wall in the 2D plan.
  • A door drawn on a wall still opens a gap in that wall in the 2D plan and the 3D pane.
  • A parallel wall a few metres away from a door is no longer cut.

RESULT

video-1211-opening-tolerance.mp4

Released to main in 6a9768f3 (release PR #1213). The fix came in through PR #1212, merged to development as b7386fee; the fix commit is 611e2001. Deploy succeeded.

Walls near a door no longer disappear on large plans. On Square One Mall V6, Level 1, Big Fat Cookies, the Escalators, the Elevators and Washroom – Men's show their whole outline again in the editor's 2D plan. A door still opens the wall it sits on.

Fix

  • New openingTolerance(model) in src/lib/floorplanEditor/floorplan/geometry.ts, the map's rule:
    • 0.6 m on a scaled plan (600 / scaleMmPerUnit);
    • 1.2 % of the larger side on an unscaled plan, the map's 0.6 m of a 50 m footprint.
  • src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/draw.ts (2D plan) and scene3d.ts (3D pane) both use it, instead of 3 % of the plan. On Square One that 3 % was 34.5 m. The 2D plan, the 3D pane and the map now cut the same openings.
  • Openings that do not sit on a wall no longer cut one. Across seven of the demo account's projects, every door and window still cuts its own wall. Three openings stop cutting a wall:
    • two doors on Square One Mall V5, about 1 m off the nearest wall;
    • one window on PT Go Thru Media, 73 units off.
      The map has never cut those either.

Tests

  • New src/lib/floorplanEditor/floorplan/__tests__/opening-tolerance.test.ts:
    • the tolerance equals the map's on scaled and unscaled plans;
    • with Square One's real coordinates, door #1 still opens its own wall but no longer Big Fat Cookies' or the Escalators'.
    • Putting the 3 % back fails all three tests.
  • pnpm test (2977), pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit and next build pass.

Checked

  • Real Chrome on a scratch copy of Square One Mall V6, Level 1, development against the fix: 4/4 (.playwright-mcp/demo/1211/check-walls.mjs). A canvas patch records which wall strokes pass through each wall's midpoint.
    • development strokes none of the five walls in the #1209 screenshot.
    • The fix strokes all five, in their rooms' colours.
    • On both, the wall under door #1 stays open.
  • Production map-thru.com after the deploy: 2/2.
    • All five walls are drawn.
    • The wall under door #1 stays open.
  • Scratch copies only; every one was deleted.
  • Demo: .playwright-mcp/demo/1211/video-1211-opening-tolerance.mp4.
  • The 3D pane uses the same helper; it was not checked pixel by pixel.

issues.display_title: Issue #1214: Viewer: hide Search Area, Direction, Event and the floor picker on a Blue Line (panorama-only) project
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

On a Blue Line project's public view, for example https://map-thru.com/v/H2s94H3V ("Pelee Island Blue Line (Demo)"), the viewer shows Search Area, Direction, Event and the floor picker. None of them has anything to offer there. Hide them.

What a Blue Line project is here

H2s94H3V is an ordinary floor map project (projectType: "floormap"). No field marks it as Blue Line. What sets it apart is its content: it is made of panoramas and nothing else.

  • 1 floor, 0 walls, 0 areas, 0 shapes, 0 access points, 0 safety markers.
  • 4 696 points, each linked to an Information record.
  • 5 718 Information records, every one a panorama (labelType: "pano", pano.tourKey set).
  • 4 671 panorama connections, 0 events.

"Clone" from a Blue Line Map (lib/blueLine/cloneProject.ts) produces the same shape: one floor of panorama points.

Today, Search lists thousands of "Panorama 4270…" rows, Direction routes between panoramas over an empty plan, Event always opens an empty list, and the floor picker holds a single floor.

Scope

  1. A project counts as panorama-only when, on every floor:
    • there are no walls, areas, shapes, access points or safety markers;
    • every point linked to an Information record links to a panorama;
    • and it has at least one such panorama.
  2. On a panorama-only project, the viewer hides Search Area, Direction, Event and the floor picker. The same applies to the public view (/v/{key}), the embed (/embed/{key}) and the owner's Preview, which share one viewer.
  3. A panorama's information card on such a project shows no "Directions" button, so Direction cannot be reached another way.
  4. Kept as is: panorama markers and the 360 view, panorama connections, the map tilt control, and the building picker (absent when the project has no building).
  5. Every other project is unchanged. Once walls, areas, other objects or non-panorama pins are added, all four controls come back.

Acceptance criteria

  • On /v/H2s94H3V, Search Area, Direction, Event and the floor picker are not shown.
  • On that project, a panorama still opens its 360 view, and its card has no Directions button.
  • A project with rooms, pins or events still shows all four controls, as before.

RESULT

video-1214-panorama-only-viewer.mp4

Released to main in 9679b41f (release PR #1216). The fix came in through PR #1215, merged to development as d586c00d; the fix commit is d8934ad4. Deploy succeeded.

https://map-thru.com/v/H2s94H3V no longer shows Search Area, Direction, Event or the floor picker. A panorama's card offers View 360 Pano without Direction.

Fix

  • New isPanoramaOnly(canvasData, informationRecords) in src/lib/preview/panoramaOnly.ts. A project counts as panorama-only when:
    • no floor has walls, areas, shapes, access points or safety markers;
    • every pin linked to an Information record is a panorama;
    • and there is at least one.
  • PreviewControls takes a panoramaOnly prop and drops the four controls. The Building picker stays.
  • PreviewOverlay computes the flag and gives the information card no Direction button on such a project.
  • /v/{key}, /embed/{key} and the owner's Preview share this viewer. Every other project is unchanged.

Tests

  • New src/lib/preview/__tests__/panoramaOnly.test.ts, plus a new case in PreviewControls.test.tsx. 14 hand-made mutants are all caught.
  • pnpm test (2983), pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit and next build pass.

Checked

  • Real Chrome on the real H2s94H3V payload, served by a local stand-in (.playwright-mcp/demo/1214/check-viewer.mjs):
    • development: all four controls, and Direction on the card;
    • the fix: none of them, View 360 Pano still opens;
    • the same project plus one room: all four controls stay (10/10).
  • Production after the deploy, 5/5: on /v/H2s94H3V, none of the four controls; a panorama's card has View 360 Pano and no Direction; the 360 view opens.
  • Demo video: .playwright-mcp/demo/1214/video-1214-panorama-only-viewer.mp4.

Not changed (already this way): the first view frames the empty plan box in the middle of the island, so no panorama is on screen until the visitor zooms out and back in on a road. A "Panorama 42709039" label also sits fixed at the centre of the screen.
